title: Levosalbutamol, salbutamol: CMDh scientific conclusions and grounds for the variation, amendments to the product information and timetable for the implementation - PSUSA/00010330/202301
authors: Coordination Group for Mutual Recognition and Decentralised Procedures – Human; Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee
journal: European Medicines Agency, PSUSA/00010330/202301, CMDh position adopted at the October 2023 meeting
funder: European Medicines Agency and the EU national competent authorities
result: On the basis of clinical trials, large population-based observational studies and a plausible mechanism of action, PRAC considered overuse of salbutamol-containing reliever medication significant and associated with deteriorating asthma control and the risk of life-threatening exacerbations, and stated that providing patients solely with salbutamol relievers leaves the underlying inflammation untreated. New section 4.4 text: overuse of short-acting beta-agonists may mask the progression of the underlying disease and contribute to deteriorating asthma control, leading to an increased risk of severe asthma exacerbations and mortality; patients who take 'as needed' salbutamol more than twice a week, not counting use before exercise, should be re-evaluated. The benefit-risk balance was judged unchanged subject to these amendments; implementation by Member States by 25 January 2024.
